rules.title: RSO annual allowable rent increase
rules.requirement: For RSO units, rent may be raised once every 12 months by the city's allowable rent increase percentage. Since February 2, 2026, landlords may no longer add an extra percentage for utilities or a 10% increase for an added dependent, though a 10% increase for an additional (non-dependent) tenant is allowed within 60 days of learning of that tenant.
rules.key_value: Once every 12 months by allowable percentage; no utility add-on after 2026-02-02
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities.
rules.coverage_text: Generally, the RSO applies to rental properties that were first built on or before October 1, 1978, as well as replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28. Covered types include apartments, condominiums, townhomes, duplexes, two or more single-family dwellings on one parcel, long-term hotel/motel rooms, residential units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs, JADUs, and mobile homes and RVs in mobile home parks. For condominiums and townhomes, rent amounts are not regulated for tenancies that began after December 31, 1995.
rules.exemptions: Rent may be reset to market rate after a voluntary move-out, certain at-fault evictions, or a tenant buyout. Rent amounts for condominiums and townhomes are not regulated for tenancies that began after December 31, 1995. A luxury exemption is available on application. LAHD-approved increases are available for capital improvements, primary renovations, seismic retrofits, rehabilitation, and just-and-reasonable returns.

rules.title: RSO legal reasons for eviction, notice and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: Landlords of RSO units may evict only for listed at-fault causes or listed no-fault causes, and no-fault evictions require tenant relocation assistance. Landlords must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict and give 30- or 60-day written notice (some cases require 120 days), and must file all termination notices with LAHD within three business days of service.
rules.key_value: 30/60-day notice (some 120-day); relocation assistance for no-fault evictions; notices filed with LAHD within 3 business days
rules.citation: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance; LAMC 151.09.C.9 & 165.05.B.5
rules.quoted_span: Give the tenant a 30-day and 60-day written notice (some evictions require 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension).
rules.coverage_text: Rental units subject to the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance.
rules.interaction: Properties not covered by the RSO are subject to the city's Just Cause Ordinance.
